title: Blob Storage -- containers, tiers, lifecycle, SAS tokens
exp: Blob Storage is Azure's S3. Same conceptual shape -- containers instead of buckets, blobs instead of objects -- with a few naming and API differences worth knowing cold.
pts: Storage Account is the top-level namespace -- one account can hold many containers, unlike S3 where bucket names are globally unique on their own.
Containers hold blobs. Blob names support '/' as a path-like convention, same as S3 keys -- no real folder structure underneath.
Access tiers: Hot (frequent), Cool (infrequent, 30-day minimum), Cold (rarer, 90-day minimum), Archive (rare, hours to rehydrate) -- directly analogous to S3 Standard/IA/Glacier/Deep Archive.
Lifecycle management policies auto-transition or delete blobs by age, defined as a JSON rule set on the Storage Account.
SAS (Shared Access Signature) tokens are Azure's presigned URL equivalent -- time-limited, permission-scoped access without sharing account keys.

ADLS Gen2 (Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2) is Blob Storage with a hierarchical namespace enabled -- this is what Databricks/Spark actually reads from in production, not plain Blob Storage, because it supports real directory-level operations Spark relies on.
code:
from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient, generate_blob_sas, BlobSasPermissions
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

client = BlobServiceClient(
    account_url="https://satishpipeline.blob.core.windows.net",
    credential=DefaultAzureCredential()
)
container = client.get_container_client("orders-raw")

with open("orders.csv", "rb") as f:
    container.upload_blob(name="2024/01/orders.csv", data=f, overwrite=True)

for blob in container.list_blobs(name_starts_with="2024/01/"):
    print(blob.name, blob.size)

sas = generate_blob_sas(
    account_name="satishpipeline", container_name="reports", blob_name="q4.pdf",
    permission=BlobSasPermissions(read=True),
    expiry=datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(hours=1)
)
url = f"https://satishpipeline.blob.core.windows.net/reports/q4.pdf?{sas}"

# Spark reads from ADLS Gen2 (hierarchical namespace), not plain Blob Storage
df = spark.read.parquet("abfss://raw@satishpipeline.dfs.core.windows.net/orders/2024/")

qa.q: What is ADLS Gen2 and why does Spark specifically need it instead of plain Blob Storage?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** ADLS Gen2 is Blob Storage with hierarchical namespace enabled -- meaning directories are real, atomic filesystem objects rather than just a naming convention over flat keys. Spark's write process (especially the rename-based commit pattern many Spark output formats use) relies on atomic directory rename operations, which plain flat Blob Storage doesn't support efficiently. Enabling hierarchical namespace on the storage account is what makes it 'ADLS Gen2' and production-ready for Spark workloads.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.

qa.q: How does a SAS token differ from an S3 presigned URL in how it's generated?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Functionally identical purpose -- time-limited, permission-scoped access to a blob without full account credentials. Generation differs: SAS tokens typically need either the storage account key or a user-delegation key obtained via Entra ID, while S3 presigned URLs are generated directly from IAM credentials. Prefer user-delegation SAS (tied to an Entra ID identity, revocable) over account-key SAS in production, since account-key SAS tokens are harder to revoke individually.
